title: Prayer and Spiritual Warfare
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Prayer and spiritual warfare teaches that prayer is a God-given means of dependence, resistance, protection, and Gospel advance in the battle against evil. Believers fight by calling on the Lord, not relying on themselves.
summary: Prayer and spiritual warfare teaches that prayer is a God-given means of dependence, resistance, protection, and Gospel advance in the battle against evil. Believers fight by calling on the Lord, not relying on themselves.
christFocus: Jesus Christ prays for His people and teaches them to pray for deliverance from evil. Through Him, believers approach the Father with confidence and receive help in the battle.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Prayer is central to spiritual warfare. After describing the armor of God, Paul calls believers to pray at all times in the Spirit with perseverance and watchfulness.

Jesus taught His disciples to pray for deliverance from evil. This shows that believers are dependent on God’s protection, wisdom, and power. Prayer is not weakness; it is faith in action.

Christ Himself prayed for Peter when Satan desired to sift him. The believer’s hope is strengthened by knowing that Jesus intercedes and that God hears the prayers of His people.

Prayer in warfare also includes Gospel mission. The church prays for boldness, open doors, deliverance from evil men, and the advance of the Word. Spiritual warfare is not only defense; it is faithful witness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Believers often try to fight spiritual battles with anxiety, effort, arguments, or isolation. Prayer brings the battle back to dependence on God.

This doctrine is especially important for the weary and tempted. Prayer keeps them near the Lord, honest about weakness, and connected to the help God provides.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Pray as one who needs God’s help. Ask for protection, discernment, repentance, courage, and Gospel fruit. Do not wait until you are overwhelmed to pray. Make prayer part of standing firm, resisting temptation, caring for others, and proclaiming Christ.
